text:
Current team members

   <a href="https://www.sacema.org/person/comfort-sunday-jones-msc/">Comfort Jones (SACEMA)</a> <a href="mailto:Comfort@sun.ac.za" class="icon-link"><i class="bi bi-envelope"></i> </a>     













Comfort Jones is a research master’s student at the South African Centre for Epidemiological Modelling and Analysis (SACEMA), Stellenbosch University, where her thesis investigates the benefits of adding wastewater surveillance in monitoring hepatitis E. In this grant, she is using wastewater data and Quality of Life (QoL) data to investigate the drivers of HEV wastewater levels we see in specific communities in Gauteng. Also, estimating the age- and sex-incidence rates for HEV in Gauteng using serology data.




   <a href="https://www.sacema.org/person/emmanuel-owusu-ahenkan-msc/">Emmanuel Owusu Ahenkan (SACEMA)</a> <a href="mailto:emowusuahenkan@gmail.com" class="icon-link"><i class="bi bi-envelope"></i> </a>     













Emmanuel Owusu Ahenkan is a PhD student at the South African Centre for Epidemiological Modelling and Analysis (SACEMA), Stellenbosch University. He holds a Master of Science degree in Mathematical Sciences and another in Machine Learning. He is passionate about applying mathematical modelling and artificial intelligence techniques to address health challenges in Africa. His research in this project focuses on modelling the impact of incorporating wastewater surveillance as a routine method for influenza control.




   Fiona Els (GCRO)     





Fiona is an epidemiologist working with the National Institute for Communicable Diseases (NICD) and the Gauteng City-Region Observatory (GCRO), to monitor pathogens in urban communities using wastewater surveillance. Fiona is a PhD candidate at the University of Witwatersrand and holds a Master of Science (MSc) in Epidemiology and Biostatistics as well as an MSc in Biochemistry. Her current research focuses on using wastewater as an environmental surveillance tool to complement clinical surveillance and determine the impact of socio-economic factors on disease. In this project, she is assisting in modelling Hepatitis A in a spatial environment.




   Laven Naidoo (GCRO)     





Dr Laven Naidoo completed his PhD in Geoinformatics at the University of Pretoria in 2017 and specialized in using Earth Observation technologies to monitor savannah, forest and wetland vegetation. Within the GCRO, he has expanded his research into the development of advanced AI/machine learning techniques, geospatial data science approaches and novel remote sensing applications within the urban environment and Sustainable Development Goals space. Such work includes the development of a carbon atlas for Gauteng, assisting in modelling econometrics and quantifying changes in the urban form. Within the context of this project, he is assisting in the development of spatial models for pathogen concentration distribution and spread and is assisting the integration of a variety of GIS and survey datasets in the project’s methodologies. He is also currently a Y-rated scientist by the South African National Research Foundation (NRF) and the convenor of the NRF Earth Sciences Ratings Panel. He is also an extraordinary lecturer at the University of Pretoria and is a MIND Fellow at the University of the Witwatersrand.




   Ntsako Mthombeni (NICD)     





Ntsako is a data analyst at the National Institute of Communicable Diseases (NICD). She holds a Master’s degree in Epidemiology and Biostatistics from the University of Cape Town, and an Environmental Health (hons) degree from the University of Johannesburg. She provides specialist back-end development and support of the data ecosystem for the Wastewater Genomics Syndicate (WGS) and the Centre for Vaccines and Immunology (CVI)’s communicable disease surveillance programmes.




   <a href="https://www.lshtm.ac.uk/aboutus/people/kathleen.oreilly">Kath O'Reilly (LSHTM)</a> <a href="mailto:emowusuahenkan@gmail.com" class="icon-link"><i class="bi bi-envelope"></i> </a>     













Kathleen O’Reilly is an Associate Professor in statistics for infectious diseases at the London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine. Dr O’Reilly is the co-Director of the internationally recognised Centre for Mathematical Modelling of Infectious Diseases (LSHTM). Her research interests are in the use of data analytics to prevent outbreaks and solve challenges in epidemiology. The research team at LSHTM are modelling partners for Unicef in the Global Polio Eradication Initiative, where analysis and modelling are used to support polio eradication challenges and inform policy. Activities in environmental and wastewater surveillance have stemmed from its use in polio eradication, and during the COVID-19 pandemic several projects were established to better understand SARS-CoV-2 spread from wastewater. In the METSI-PH consortia Kath is supporting the research of several group members, including PhD and MSc supervision. Additionally, Kath will develop research in how vale of information methods can be used to evaluate wastewater data.

   Mukhlid Yousif (NICD)     





Dr Mukhlid Yousif is a Researcher, and Senior Genomics and Public Health Scientist with over 15 years of experience in molecular virology, bioinformatics, and genomic epidemiology. His research spans hepatitis B virus, HIV drug resistance, measles, rubella, and polio. He co-established the Wastewater Genomics Syndicate at the National Institute for Communicable Diseases (NICD) in South Africa, leading the development and implementation of multi-pathogen wastewater surveillance to inform public health responses. Dr Yousif has led international collaborations and consortia, received multiple grants, published over 20 peer-reviewed articles, supervised postgraduate students, and works closely with regional and global partners to strengthen diseases surveillance using wastewater across Africa.
